intro.body: Seasonal flu vaccination helps reduce the risk of catching flu and can lessen illness if you do become unwell.
Many people consider a flu vaccination each year as part of sensible winter health planning.
A brief assessment checks whether vaccination is suitable for you and explains what to expect.
Flu vaccination complements wider healthcare, with clear guidance when GP or urgent care is more appropriate.
Plain-language information helps you decide whether to contact the pharmacy about flu vaccination.

problem.heading: Why Flu Vaccination Matters
problem.body: Flu can cause significant illness during winter months. Vaccination is a practical way to reduce risk for many people.

problem.heading: Understanding Suitability
problem.body: Not everyone can receive a flu vaccination in every setting. Suitability depends on your health, medicines and current circumstances.

problem.heading: Common Questions
problem.body: People often want clarity on suitability, timing and how the service is arranged before contacting the pharmacy.

problem.heading: Getting The Right Care
problem.body: Flu vaccination is one part of winter health planning. The pharmacy can advise on suitability and signpost when other care is more appropriate.

benefits.heading: Why People Consider Vaccination
benefits.body: Flu vaccination offers a straightforward way to reduce seasonal flu risk with clear guidance on next steps.

benefits.heading: What You Can Expect
benefits.body: A structured discussion covering suitability, the vaccination process and sensible aftercare.

benefits.heading: Practical Advantages
benefits.body: Community access can make it easier to fit flu vaccination around everyday commitments.

benefits.heading: Patient-Focused Support
benefits.body: Clear information helps you understand suitability and what to do after vaccination.

benefits.heading: Accessible Healthcare
benefits.body: Community settings can put flu vaccination closer to where people live and work.

eligibility.heading: Who Can Use This Service
eligibility.body: Suitability for flu vaccination is confirmed individually. Contact the pharmacy to check whether vaccination is appropriate for you.

eligibility.heading: Is This Right For Me
eligibility.body: If you are unsure whether flu vaccination is suitable, contact the pharmacy for guidance.

eligibility.heading: Before you contact the pharmacy
eligibility.body: Having basic health information ready can help the pharmacy advise you.

eligibility.heading: Checking Suitability
eligibility.body: Contact the pharmacy if unsure — they can advise on the best pathway for your situation.

eligibility.heading: When To Wait
eligibility.body: If you feel acutely unwell, suitability may need to be reviewed before vaccination can go ahead.

howItWorks.heading: How The Service Works
howItWorks.body: Contact the pharmacy to confirm how flu vaccination is arranged locally. If suitable, you receive assessment and vaccination with clear advice on next steps.

howItWorks.heading: Assessment Steps
howItWorks.body: The assessment covers relevant health information, confirms suitability and explains the vaccination process before proceeding.

howItWorks.heading: The Vaccination Process
howItWorks.body: Where suitable, vaccination is given with clear aftercare guidance and advice on when to seek further help.

howItWorks.heading: During your visit
howItWorks.body: Allow time to ask questions and receive clear aftercare guidance.

howItWorks.heading: After Your Visit
howItWorks.body: Follow aftercare advice given. Seek GP or urgent care if you develop concerning symptoms after vaccination or feel seriously unwell.

preparationGuide.heading: Preparing For Your Visit
preparationGuide.body: Bring a medicines list, notes about allergies and any questions you want to ask.
bullets: Loose clothing for upper arm access

preparationGuide.heading: What To Bring
preparationGuide.body: A medicines list, allergy information and any questions you want to ask about flu vaccination.

preparationGuide.heading: Consultation tips
preparationGuide.body: Wear loose clothing with easy access to your upper arm and allow time to ask questions.

preparationGuide.heading: Making The Most Of Your Visit
preparationGuide.body: Honest answers about your health help ensure safe care — ask about aftercare and when to seek help before you leave.

trustSafety.heading: Safety Considerations
trustSafety.body: Flu vaccination is not suitable for everyone. Care falls outside pharmacy scope when symptoms suggest urgent medical review is needed.

trustSafety.heading: When To Seek GP Or Urgent Care
trustSafety.body: Severe, persistent or worsening symptoms and emergency presentations need medical review beyond routine vaccination.

trustSafety.heading: After Vaccination
trustSafety.body: Most people tolerate flu vaccination well. Follow aftercare advice and report any unexpected reactions promptly.
bullets: Keep a note of vaccination date

patientEducation.heading: Understanding Flu Vaccination
patientEducation.body: Flu vaccination helps your immune system recognise flu viruses. It reduces the likelihood and severity of flu for many people.

patientEducation.heading: Why Annual Vaccination
patientEducation.body: Flu viruses change over time. Updated vaccines are developed for each season.

patientEducation.heading: What To Expect After Vaccination
patientEducation.body: Some people notice mild soreness or tiredness for a short time. Serious reactions are uncommon.

patientEducation.heading: When Vaccination May Not Be Suitable
patientEducation.body: Some health conditions or medicines affect suitability. Individual assessment confirms whether vaccination is appropriate.

mythVsFact.heading: Myths Vs Facts
bullets: Myth: Flu vaccination gives you flu. Fact: Vaccines used in the UK do not contain live flu virus.
Myth: Healthy people do not need vaccination. Fact: Anyone can catch flu; vaccination reduces risk.
Myth: One vaccination lasts forever. Fact: Seasonal vaccines are updated each year.

mythVsFact.heading: Common Misconceptions
bullets: Myth: The service is always available without contact. Fact: Contacting the pharmacy may be required.
Myth: Online advice is enough. Fact: Suitability must be confirmed individually.

mythVsFact.heading: Service Facts
bullets: Myth: Vaccination suits everyone. Fact: Individual assessment confirms suitability.
Myth: Same service everywhere. Fact: Local service arrangements vary.
Myth: Side effects should be ignored. Fact: Report concerns promptly.

mythVsFact.heading: Safe Use Clarified
bullets: Myth: Emergency care at pharmacy. Fact: Emergencies need 999 or A&E.
Myth: Vaccination replaces GP care. Fact: Services complement wider healthcare.
Myth: Skip follow-up if feeling fine. Fact: Follow aftercare advice given.

faqs.answer: Contact the pharmacy to confirm how the service is currently arranged.

faqs.question: What applies locally for flu vaccinations?
faqs.answer: Contact the pharmacy to confirm how the service is currently arranged.

faqs.question: What should I bring to my flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Bring a medicines list, allergy information and any questions you want to ask about the service.

faqs.question: Who can have a flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Suitability is checked individually. Contact the pharmacy to confirm whether vaccination is appropriate for you.

faqs.question: Can I speak to someone before arranging a flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Contact the pharmacy to confirm how the service is currently arranged.

faqs.question: What if flu vaccination is not suitable for me?
faqs.answer: You receive guidance on appropriate next steps, which may include signposting to other care when needed.

faqs.question: What happens during flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Relevant health information is reviewed, suitability is confirmed, and vaccination is given where appropriate, with aftercare advice.

faqs.question: When should I see a GP instead of having a flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: If you have severe or worsening symptoms, or feel seriously unwell, seek GP or urgent care rather than routine vaccination.

faqs.question: What follow-up is needed after flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Follow aftercare advice. Contact the pharmacy or your GP if you have unexpected reactions or concerns.
